setting: A fictional meeting with a prospective customer who wants to hear how your team works.

presentation.situation: {{name}} is considering working with your company, and asks for a true story that shows {{value}}. Tell a short professional story from your own work or studies. Do not invent achievements.
presentation.opening: Before we decide, I'd love to hear a real story that shows how you handle {{value}}.

brief.you_are: You are telling a prospective customer a true professional story.
brief.situation: {{name}} is considering working with your company, and asks for a true story that shows {{value}}. Tell a short professional story from your own work or studies. Do not invent achievements.
brief.task: Tell a clear story with a beginning, middle and end, include real details, and say why it matters to them.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} remembers your story and understands what it says about {{value}}.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are telling a prospective customer a true professional story.
goals: Tell a clear story with a beginning, middle and end, include real details, and say why it matters to them.

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: Is deciding whether to work with your company

card.want: To see what your company is really like when things get difficult.
card.attitude: Interested and slightly sceptical of sales talk.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Ask 'what does that mean for me?'
Never supply details of the story

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: {{name}} wants a true story that shows {{value}}.
The story comes from the speaker. {{name}} knows only what the speaker says.

objectives.description: Tell a story with a clear beginning and end
objectives.evidence: The learner tells events in order, with a beginning and a turning point.
alternatives: Last year we had a client whose launch was at risk. Then...

objectives.evidence: The learner includes a concrete detail or evidence.
alternatives: We had three days, and the file was missing.

objectives.description: Say why it matters to the listener
objectives.evidence: The learner connects the story to the listener.
alternatives: What that means for you is that you will always get a straight answer.

examples: Last year, a client's launch was at risk. Then we...
We had three days, and we called the client each morning.
What that means for you is that you will always know where things stand.

beats.goal: Hear a story with a shape.
beats.orient: Tell me a true story from your work or studies. Start with when it happened, and what went wrong.
Add a real detail from your story: a number, a name or something somebody said.

signals: \b(?:means for you|for you|that'?s why|the lesson|what (?:this|that) (?:shows|means)|so you)\b
opportunity: So what does that mean for me?
Why are you telling me this?
beats.orient: Finish by saying why this story matters to me. Start with: What that means for you is.
fallback: Why are you telling me this?
So what does that mean for me?

closing_line: Thank you. That helps me a lot more than a brochure would.

o1.good: A clear beginning, a problem and what came next.
o1.micro_lesson: Start with a time and a problem.
o1.model: Last year, a client's launch was at risk. Then we...

o2.good: One real detail makes a story believable.
o2.model: We had three days, and we called the client each morning.

o3.good: Ending with the point for this listener.
o3.micro_lesson: Say: What that means for you is.
o3.model: What that means for you is that you will always know where things stand.
o3.smaller_step: Say: What that means for you.
